sections.html:
The Weld County Clerk and Recorder works from 1250 H Street in Greeley. Mail goes to PO Box 459, Greeley, CO 80632. You can reach the office at (970) 304-6530 or crstaff@weld.gov, and it is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

One detail matters on closing day. The county's recording FAQ says documents accepted after 4:30 p.m. count as the next day's business, so a deed dropped off late in the afternoon will not be recorded that day.

Recording a letter or legal size document costs $43.00 whatever its page count. When a document conveys real property for more than $500, the state's documentary fee is added at $.01 per $100 of the sale price. Weld County adds no transfer tax of its own, so the documentary fee is the only transfer-related charge you will see here.

Document or serviceWeld County fee
Letter or legal size document$43.00 regardless of pages

The fee schedule is set by statute. Documents that arrive with too little money come back unrecorded. Make checks payable to the Weld County Clerk and Recorder or to WCCR, and sign them.

sections.h2: What a deed needs before the clerk will accept it
sections.html:
Rejected documents almost always trace back to the short list below. The county's recording page lays out what to check.

  • Margins: at least one inch at the top and bottom and half an inch on the left and right (C.R.S. 30-10-406(3)(a)).
  • Grantee address: every deed carries the grantee's legal mailing address (C.R.S. 38-35-109(2)), because that address is where future tax statements go.
  • Legibility: a poor original makes a poor public record, and an illegible document is recorded as received with a clerk's note.
  • Return address: mark where the recorded original should be sent.
  • Order: when you submit several documents, stack them in the order you want them recorded.
  • No personal data: recorded documents are public, so keep Social Security numbers and similar details off them.

Clerks do not give legal advice, prepare or notarize documents, or keep blank forms on hand. Recording a document also does not make it legal or authentic, so have the deed drawn up by a title company or attorney.

sections.h2: Which county should record my deed?
sections.html:
The county where the land lies records the deed. Weld's own page cautions that a document sent to the wrong county is not rejected, and the recording fees are not refunded. Check the legal description and the county before anything goes in the mail.

This comes up often in Weld because several towns cross county lines. Windsor, Johnstown, Erie, Berthoud, Lochbuie, Longmont, Brighton, Northglenn and Thornton each have a portion in a neighboring county. A Windsor parcel might be in Weld or in Larimer, and that county's recorder takes the deed.

sections.h2: Finding an owner or a recorded document
sections.html:
Ownership lookups go through the County Assessor, whose website has a Property Information and Mapping section. The Assessor is at 1400 N 17th Avenue in Greeley, phone (970) 353-3845. Recorded documents are searched through the county's self-service website.

The online index search is free. Viewing and printing images costs money, charged either by monthly fee or per document. Online copies are $.50 for the first page and $.25 for each added page, and a certified online copy adds $1.00 per document. Sellers sometimes pull the recorded vesting deed to confirm how title is held, and that search is a good first step when an inherited house has no clear paperwork. Staff can point you to the self-service site if you get stuck.

sections.h2: Releasing a deed of trust and paying the tax bill
sections.html:
Neither of those jobs falls to the recorder. The Weld County Public Trustee releases a deed of trust, and the Weld County Treasurer answers tax questions. Both are in the building at 1400 N. 17th Avenue in Greeley, reachable at (970) 400-3290.

When a loan is paid off at a sale, the lender's release goes through the Public Trustee, and the title company usually tracks it. A change of name on the tax roll follows the deed: the Treasurer says a name change can only be made by deed, and the Assessor updates the name once the deed is recorded with the Clerk and Recorder.

Weld County covers 4,017 square miles with Greeley as its seat, third in Colorado by area. The 2020 census counted 328,981 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 378,426. Farms and oil and gas share the county with fast-growing Front Range suburbs, so a seller in a small eastern town and a seller near Interstate 25 face different buyer pools, though both record at the same Greeley office.

sections.h2: A cash sale and the recording steps
sections.html:
A cash sale uses the same recording steps as any other. The seller signs a deed, the title company confirms the legal description and the grantee address, pays the recording and documentary fees, and the clerk records it. With no buyer's lender, there is no underwriting or appraisal to wait for, so a cash closing can be scheduled quickly once title is clear.

If you own a Weld County house and want to sell as is, send us the address and we will reply with a written cash offer. If the house needs work, has tenants or came to you through an estate, mention that in your first message. None of those facts changes where the deed is recorded, but they do change what the title company must collect before it can close.

A few habits keep recording smooth. Ask the title company which county will record the deed. Confirm that the grantee's mailing address appears on it. Verify that fees are paid by a signed check made out to the right payee, and aim to have the deed at the clerk's office well before 4:30 p.m. If you are paying off a loan, ask who is requesting the release from the Public Trustee and when you can expect confirmation. Finally, keep a copy of the recorded deed once it comes back, since it is the record of the transfer.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Weld County, Colorado?
faqs.a: It costs $43.00 for a letter or legal size document regardless of page count. The state documentary fee of $.01 per $100 of sale price is added when the price is over $500.

faqs.q: What is the Weld County Clerk and Recorder's address?
faqs.a: The office is at 1250 H Street in Greeley, with a mailing address of PO Box 459, Greeley, CO 80632. The phone number is (970) 304-6530.

faqs.q: Does Weld County charge a transfer tax?
faqs.a: No county transfer tax applies. The only transfer-related charge is the state documentary fee of $.01 per $100 of price on documents conveying real property for more than $500.

faqs.q: What happens if I record a deed in the wrong county?
faqs.a: Weld County does not reject documents meant for another county and does not refund recording fees, so confirm the county and legal description first.

faqs.q: What does a Colorado deed need to show about the buyer?
faqs.a: It must show the grantee's legal mailing address, as C.R.S. 38-35-109(2) requires, so tax statements can reach the new owner.
